requirement: Each assessment’s usage record MUST report its validator’s `prepared_inputs` and `delivered_inputs` under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats`. It MUST also report the invocation count and total result bytes for each invoked tool under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.calls` and {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.result_bytes`.
rationale:
Add a marked test (`requirements.authoring.usage_inputs`) in `tests/authoring_cli.rs` where a model response includes a tool call that the harness skips, for example a call that follows `submit_result` in the same turn. Assert that `provider_usage.tools` leaves that tool's `calls` and `result_bytes` unchanged, and that `prepared_inputs` and `delivered_inputs` are unchanged. — `requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.calls` says skipped calls leave usage unchanged. This is an explicit unchanged-value obligation, so it needs a test. The reviewed tests are `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free`, `a_successful_retry_reports_partial_token_measurements`, `terminal_provider_failure_retains_the_retry_and_undelivered_inputs`, `each_edge_result_counts_once_and_a_failed_lookup_only_charges_tool_usage` and `listing_charges_result_bytes_while_only_the_explicit_read_adds_an_input`. None of them issues a skipped call. A harness that charges skipped calls for `calls` or `result_bytes` would pass all five.

Add a marked test that exercises paged results, where a `get_next_page` continuation returns a further page of `read_node` or search results, and also a `search_structure` call. Assert the `prepared_inputs` and `delivered_inputs` counts: one per requested `read_node` page, one per excerpt on a requested search page, and each input counted once. Assert the `get_next_page` and `search_structure` `calls` and `result_bytes`. The assertions should use a result that contains non-ASCII text, so the UTF-8 byte length differs from the character count. — `requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats` counts each requested `read_node` page and each excerpt on a requested search page. The reviewed tests only use single-page `read_node` and `outgoing_edges` results and one `search_text` page. The tool list shows `get_next_page` and `search_structure` exist, but no reviewed test calls either. If continuation pages or structural-search excerpts were uncounted or double-counted, the tests would still pass. `ToolUsage.result_bytes` requires the UTF-8 byte length, but every asserted result is ASCII, where a character count would match `.len()`. A paging unit test in `src/authoring/pages.rs` appears to exist. It is not marked for `requirements.authoring.usage_inputs` and does not assert usage totals.

text: Each assessment’s usage record MUST report its validator’s `prepared_inputs` and `delivered_inputs` under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.UsageStats`. It MUST also report the invocation count and total result bytes for each invoked tool under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.calls` and {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.running-criteria.ToolUsage.result_bytes`.

`UsageStats` exposes the following totals. `attempts` counts each request sent to the provider once. `retries` counts attempts that repeat a failed request. `failed_attempts` counts attempts that returned a provider error, including those followed by a successful retry.

`prepared_inputs` counts inputs prepared for agent messages. Each node inserted in the opening message counts once. Each requested `read_node` page and each `outgoing_edges` result counts once, including repeated reads. A requested search page counts one input per excerpt on that page. Source listings, search finalization, and opaque custom-tool results contribute zero.

`delivered_inputs` counts those inputs when the provider first responds successfully to the request carrying them. Each input counts once across retries and subsequent turns that replay the same conversation history. For example, if the opening message supplies three nodes and the provider fails permanently before replying, usage records three prepared inputs and zero delivered inputs.
Each invocation increments the tool’s `calls` by one, including an invocation that returns an error. Skipped calls leave usage unchanged.

Each invocation adds the UTF-8 byte length of its result text to the tool’s `result_bytes`, measured before the provider encodes the request. Error messages count by the same rule. An invocation that produces no result text adds zero bytes.
